subject: Intermittent on-prem -> VPC path: reachability checklist and MSS/SG mitigation playbook

Subject: Intermittent reachability to VPC after private deployment cutover

Jordan —

We flipped over to the new private attachment last night (per the runbook) and since ~20:30PT we've seen intermittent failures from our replication cluster to the Redwood VPC. Symptoms: TCP sessions stall around 1400-1500B, some restarts, and occasional 504s in our app logs. We attached a short tcpdump from the edge appliance (blackthorn_tcpdump_cutover.pcap) and a traceroute (edge-trace-2026-09-20.txt).

We tried reducing MTU on the on-prem host but the problem persisted until we forced a TCP MSS-clamp on the appliance, which improved throughput briefly. We suspect a mix of MTU + conntrack behavior on our ASA firewall and potentially a security-group rule that is not allowing ephemeral port ranges from your edge.

Can Redwood ops help validate packet flows from egress in your VPC and share any known SG/conntrack limits to watch for? This is impacting our nightly ingest window — any help appreciated.

Thanks,
Alan Ross
NetOps Lead, Blackthorn Analytics

Thanks Alan — looping in Marissa and Karthik from Private Deploy/Network Ops to help triage.

Quick asks so we can prioritize:
- Can you confirm the exact on-prem edge model and OS + current conntrack limits? (ASA version or vendor appliance)
- Do you have stats/graphs for conntrack table usage around the cutover window?
- Example application socket states (SYN_SENT/SYN_RECV/RST) from the host would help.

Marissa/Karthik — from the traces Alan shared I see MTU-size stalls and the MSS-clamp helping. Please review the attached pcap and traceroute and advise if this looks like a PMTUD drop, an SG block on ephemeral ports, or a conntrack exhaustion symptom. If multiple mitigations are needed, propose an ordered playbook we can present to the customer for a 1-hour change window: 1) MSS clamp at on-prem egress, 2) SG ephemeral port allow on VPC edge, 3) conntrack tuning on appliance, 4) revert plan.

Alan — we can also kick off a quick packet capture at our egress side if you authorize.

—Jordan

Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 00:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent reachability to VPC after private deployment cutover

Thanks Alan — I dug into the pcap and traceroute overnight. Highlights:

- Evidence of PMTUD black-holing: we see ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages not reaching the sender on several flows (likely dropped by the on-prem ASA due to ICMP policy). Packets from the host with DF set are going to the edge and then get dropped beyond the RI edge when larger than ~1400B.
- When you temporarily applied MSS clamp on the appliance we saw successful flows up to ~1380B. That lines up with PMTUD failing and MSS-clamp acting as a stop-gap.
- Separately, we observed a surge of TCP connections from the replication cluster that correlate with conntrack table growth on your appliance. The pcap contains repeated SYN retries; some flows show mid-connection RSTs, suggesting state race or hit conntrack limit.
- I also spot a security-group on the Redwood edge that only allows established connections but we do not see an explicit allow for the ephemeral port ranges from your public egress IPs in the current ACL set. If the edge drops initial SYNs (or blocks ICMP), that compounds the PMTUD/conntrack effect.

Proposed ordered playbook (minimal blast radius):
1) Schedule 30-min change window.
2) On your appliance: temporarily set MSS-clamp to 1360 for the replication subnet (quick rollback command ready). This is low-risk and should restore steady traffic while we diagnose.
3) On Blackthorn ASA: increase conntrack/hash buckets and ephemeral port range if the platform config allows; bump conntrack timeout for SYN_RECV to reduce churn. If vendor appliance needs a reboot for changes, schedule that out of peak.
4) On Redwood edge: add a short-lived allow rule for Blackthorn egress IPs for ephemeral port range 32768-60999 (we will remove after validation) and ensure ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages are accepted through the edge path.
5) Capture bi-directional tcpdumps on both sides for 15 minutes post-change and collect conntrack metrics.

Attachments: I exported a small annotated trace snippet to edge-trace-2026-09-20.txt showing the PMTUD failure points.

If we want a lower-impact first step, we can do only (2) MSS-clamp + capture, then proceed to (3)/(4) if problems persist. I'm happy to own coordination and rollbacks.

-Marissa
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

We're in the 02:30 PT window right now — if you can act quickly we can validate before our morning ingest.

—Alan

Follow-up and summary for the runbook we'll execute in the 10:00-11:00 PT change window:

1) Quick mitigation (now): Blackthorn applies MSS-clamp 1360 on the replication subnet egress — Alan confirmed this is done. Collect 15 minutes of tcpdump and conntrack stats (Alan to share).
2) If mitigation succeeds: Redwood will add a temporary SG allow for Blackthorn egress IPs (ephemeral ports 32768-60999) at the edge. This rule will be logged and auto-removed after 2 hours.
3) If we still see failures: Blackthorn to schedule conntrack/table resizing on ASA during a maintenance window; Redwood will hold a standby rollback to remove SG change.
4) Validation: compare pre/post tcpdumps and watch application metrics; document traces into JIRA-5691 and attach the captures.

Karthik & Mina, please prepare:
- Standard ASA commands for increasing conntrack/hash and ephemeral range (include vendor notes if reboot required).
- Redwood edge change snippet to add temporary SG allowance + verification commands and a CloudWatch/observability link we can monitor.

Marissa — thanks for the annotated trace. Alan — once you share the 15-minute capture we will run the edge-side pcap and make a final call for the conntrack maintenance.

I'll update JIRA-5691 with this playbook and link the captures.

—Jordan
